messages:
emma_csm: FYI — Acme Legal escalated: after last night's variant swap they see many 'legal citation' style references the model is inventing. They included 3 examples.
jamal_support: can you paste one of the failing prompts + the model's output? also which customer plan/tenant? :thinking_face:
emma_csm: Tenant: acme-legal-prod. Prompt and output below (redacted client data):\n\nPrompt:\n```\n"Summarize the 2012 Smith v. Darrow ruling and list precedent cases relevant to contract formation in tech services."\n```
Model output (returned 2024-11-05T02:14:03Z):\n```\n"Smith v. Darrow (2012) established the three-part test for digital contract formation; see also United States v. Filer (2009) and Eastern District v. Halden (2010). Court concluded that implicit click-through constitutes assent where ..."\n```
Note: those case names (United States v. Filer, Eastern District v. Halden) are fabricated — customer checked and couldn't find them.
triage-bot: Incident candidate created: INC-2948 (auto-detected pattern: factuality_regression). Tags: customer-impact, post-rollout
eng-ml-oncall: thanks. Which model variant was serving for that tenant at the time? any routing changes or canary completed last night?
emma_csm: We pushed a rollout at 23:40 UTC: routing default changed from `redwood-2.3-stable` -> `redwood-2.4-latency-qa` for 50% of requests (canary -> full at 00:30 UTC). Customer reported issues starting ~01:30 UTC. They say overall latency dropped ~15% but these fabricated references started appearing.
jamal_support: do we have the exact request_id / response payload from their repro? we need full headers + model_name + token counts.
emma_csm: gave them a repro curl earlier; here's the minimal repro we asked them to run and sample output they pasted:\n```\ncurl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2.4-latency-qa","input":"Summarize the 2012 Smith v. Darrow ruling...","max_tokens":300,"temperature":0.0}'\n```
Response snippet:\n```\n{"id":"r-abc123","model":"redwood-2.4-latency-qa","output":"Smith v. Darrow (2012) ... United States v. Filer (2009) ..."}\n```
alex_runtime: please check if the routing policy fell back to a quantized variant (we recently deployed a quantization profile change that affects kernel selection). sometimes Oracle-like citations pop up after pruning/quantization mismatch.
eng-ml-oncall: good call. Also check compilation/kernel selection logs for that model hash around 23:35-00:45 UTC. if a different kernel path was chosen it could change tokenization/weight numerics -> hallucination surface.
sara_pm: customer is asking for rollback if we can't show a plan within 24h. they say this is blocking their compliance review.
jamal_support: marking P1 for customer-impact; adding notes to INC-2948. can we do a quick A/B check: run the same prompt against previous variant `redwood-2.3-stable` and `redwood-2.4-latency-qa` on our side and capture top 5 completions with temperature 0?
eng-ml-oncall: I'll kick off an eval run on the legal prompt set now and capture logits / ngram differences. also will dump KV cache usage and tokenization diffs. link to run: https://internal.redwood/run/INC-2948-eval (internal)
emma_csm: customer provided 3 more examples, same pattern: authoritative-sounding but unverifiable citations. they also said the model sometimes invents publication dates for real cases.
alex_runtime: checking autoscaling and prefix cache invalidation for acme-legal-prod tenant — if prefix cache was cleared mid-rollout, that could expose cold-cache behaviors that amplify hallucinations.
eng-ml-oncall: next steps: 1) reproduce locally against both variants (in progress) 2) check model binary hash & kernel logs (in progress) 3) run eval sweep and produce diff report (eta 2-3h) 4) if repro confirmed and degradation > threshold -> revert routing (canary rollback) and notify CSM. tagging @sara_pm for rollback decision.
sara_pm: thanks — if the eval shows factuality drop > 8% on legal prompt suite we should rollback. please update customer with interim note and ETA.
emma_csm: sent interim note to Acme Legal: "we're investigating; we've paused any further expansion of the variant and will update by EOD." they replied :eyes: and asked to be kept in loop.
jamal_support: I'll coordinate customer comms and collect their raw request_ids. please add any matching request_ids to INC-2948.
triage-bot: INC-2948 status updated to Investigating. Priority: P1. Assigned: eng-ml-oncall, alex_runtime, jamal_support.
eng-ml-oncall: quick datapoint — initial eval run shows redwood-2.4-latency-qa has a measurable uptick in hallucination tokens on the legal prompt set vs redwood-2.3-stable. saving full report to ticket.
alex_runtime: prepping a rollback playbook in case we need to revert routing. want to avoid full rollback if we can patch config (quantization/compilation flags) quickly.
emma_csm: customer asked if this could be related to the 'latency-optimizations' flag you enabled last month. they are concerned tradeoff lost them accuracy.
eng-ml-oncall: could be. we'll examine model config diffs: temperature, repetition_penalty, logits_bias, prefix sampling, tokenizer changes. I'll post diffs in the ticket.
sara_pm: good. keep me posted. if you need a hotfix rollout window please propose one and I'll coordinate with infra.
jamal_support: adding meeting for 30 mins to align on rollback criteria and comms: 10:30 UTC. invite sent.
emma_csm: thanks team. customer is breathing down for a resolution; they value the latency improvement but not at the cost of fabricated legal refs. :warning:
